summary: Add host by IP + root password: Controller pushes an existing site-bound enrollment token to a reachable host's local API (POST /api/local/v1/enrollment) after operator fingerprint confirmation (POST /api/v1/hosts/probe, POST /api/v1/sites/{id}/hosts), replacing the manual nex-core-agent enroll step for reachable hosts while keeping it as a documented fallback. API impact: new contract (probeHost, addSiteHost, localEnroll); the underlying token/certificate contract (createEnrollmentToken, agent.Enroll, POST /api/v1/agent/enroll) is reused unchanged.

guide.reason: The operator-facing Add host workflow changed from a manual token + CLI step to an address/root-password panel with fingerprint confirmation; the manual token flow remains documented as the fallback for unreachable hosts, and new error cases (fingerprint mismatch, wrong password, host unreachable, already enrolled, revoked-host re-enrollment) needed troubleshooting entries.

api.reason: Three new operations (probeHost, addSiteHost, localEnroll) are documented in both OpenAPI contracts, regenerated into their HTML references, and given a dedicated docs/API.md section covering auth, validation, errors, retry/outage behavior and version compatibility with hosts/Controllers that lack the new routes.

verification.method: Real lab walkthrough passed 2026-09-09: tests/integration/add_host_lab.py ran 12 checks with real Chromium against the disposable nested-KVM lab (Nex Core host 10.0.2.15, Controller appliance 10.0.2.20 running the working-tree Controller rebuilt in debian:13-slim): probe fingerprint verified against the host's served certificate, wrong fingerprint 502 before login, wrong password 401, already-enrolled 409, non-revoked re-enrollment 409, revoke then browser re-enrollment keeping identity and pool, retry 409, audit without passwords; plus a fresh enrollment through a second isolated nex-core-local instance (auto-created pool with the host as master, in-process agent reporting fresh), a nex-core-local restart, and journal hygiene. Lab preparation caught a real bug hidden by the unit tests: the push sent the host-identity CA as trust while the appliance serves a self-signed HTTPS certificate; fixed by pushing the Controller's served certificate (cmd/nex-controller/main.go reads -tls-cert into Config.ServerCertPEM) with 503 when absent, and TestAddSiteHostSuccess now uses a self-signed listener that fails on the old value. Local checks after the fix: go test -race ./..., python3 scripts/generate_api.py --check, python3 -m unittest discover -s tests, npm --prefix web run typecheck/build, python3 scripts/check_docs.py --all, and tests/integration/phase1.py --browser all pass. Not covered: package upgrade, physical hardware, other L2 segments, manual fallback in the lab.
